units.en: ⟦0⟧ is a minor country in Northern Europe with a population of ⟦1⟧. It borders ⟦2⟧ to the north, ⟦3⟧ to the northwest, with the Baltic Sea to the south and west. To the east lies the ⟦4⟧, which may put pressure on Finland's eastern regions.

⟦0⟧ was a large yet culturally independent region of ⟦1⟧ first attached in the early 12th century. Finland was ceded to Russia after the Finnish War of 1809. Following the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 and Russia's internal turmoil Finland declared itself independent. After a brief yet very destructive civil war in 1918 Finland was formally recognized as an independent nation.

After 20 years of independence Finland was attacked by the ⟦0⟧ in 1939, leading to the Winter War. Against all odds the badly outnumbered and under-equipped Finnish army was able to repel the Soviet attacks until a grand offensive in 1940 finally forced the country to sue for peace. Finland lost about 11% of its territory (equivalent to the states of Salla and Karjala in-game) but survived as an independent nation, unlike the Baltic states which were annexed into the Soviet Union later in 1940.

After the ⟦0⟧'s invasion and occupation of ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ in 1940 through Operation Weserübung, and the subsequent fall of ⟦3⟧ in the same year, Finland was left geopolitically isolated; the British and Americans were too far away, Sweden was unwilling to compromise its neutrality and allying with the Soviet Union was impossible. Left with no other viable options, Finland begun to approach Germany, signing various cooperation and defense agreements, in hopes of preserving its independence and hopefully regaining its lost territories, but crucially, Finland did not sign the Tripartite Pact and did not fully join the Axis at any point.

In 1941, when Germany launched Operation Barbarossa and made war against the Soviet Union, Finland joined the offensive as a co-belligerent - officially after Soviet bombers struck Finnish military air fields from which German bombers were attacking Leningrad - to reconquer its lost territories, initially calling the conflict the "Summer War". After it was clear that Operation Barbarossa was unsuccessful it was renamed to the Continuation War. During this conflict Finland fought as a co-belligerent to the German Reich and ⟦0⟧ and invaded eastern Karelia (equivalent to the states of Onega and Olonets in-game) in addition to reconquering the territory lost during the Winter War. Despite pressure from Germany, Finland refused to attack Leningrad or sever the Murmansk railway and fought the Continuation War separately from Germany. The conquest of eastern Karelia and the seemingly unstoppable Wehrmacht led many in the Finns to dream of a ⟦1⟧ encompassing perhaps even all of Scandinavia and the Baltic states.

In 1944, a Soviet grand offensive involving a force larger than the Allied invasion force of D-Day forced the Finns to fall back, but the Finnish forces managed to stop the Soviet attack in the battles of Tali-ihantala, Vuosalmi-Äyräpää and Viipuri bay before soviet forces reached the border of the Moscow peace treaty in the Karelian Isthmus. Through some political finesse, Finland was able to disengage itself from its obligations to Germany and signed an armistice with the Soviet Union in early 1945, making Finland the last sovereign axis-aligned nation in Europe to surrender before the fall of Nazi Germany. One of the conditions of the ceasefire was that the Finns had to expel all remaining German soldiers from Finnish soil, which, after some reluctance, was done during in the Lapland War. After this the Second World War was finally over for Finland's part. A final peace treaty with the rest of the Allies was signed in 1947. Of note, Finland was one of only three European nations involved in the Second World War that survived the entire war without its capital being occupied even once, be it during or after the war, with the other two being the ⟦0⟧ and Finland's chief enemy, the Soviet Union.

⟦0⟧ gets a unique national focus tree as part of the ⟦1⟧ expansion. Without the expansion, Finland doesn't have access to the unhistorical branches of the national focus tree.
The Finnish national focus tree can be divided into 6 branches and 10 subbranches:
This allows the player to install a socialist government and depending on which path the player takes, makes Finland ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧. This branch requires ⟦2⟧
This installs a ⟦0⟧ government in Finland after a Civil War. The bottom section creates ⟦1⟧ and requires joining the Comintern. This sub-branch requires ⟦2⟧
Approach the Soviets/Antagonize the Soviets Sub-branch

The ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ shared sub-branch allows the player to chose whether to ally or antagonize the ⟦2⟧. The bottom section creates a faction with other Nordic and Baltic countries rather than ally with the major factions. It also creates the ⟦3⟧ and allows the coring of Finnic states under the former ⟦4⟧. This sub-branch requires ⟦5⟧
This installs a ⟦0⟧ government in Finland. The bottom section creates the ⟦1⟧ and allows Finland to Join the Allies. This sub-branch requires ⟦2⟧
Align the Agrarian League/The Finnish Swedish Peoples Party Sub-branch
The shared ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ focuses gives political advisors as well as increase Public Trust.

The Historical ⟦0⟧ branch seeks alliances in either the Allies, the Axis, or a Nordic Alliance in preparation for ⟦1⟧ threat. The left path gives industrial bonuses and bonuses to the country leader. The right path gives Finland the decision to foment uprisings in ⟦2⟧

This hidden focus turns Finland into a ⟦0⟧ as the ⟦1⟧ and installs Prince Wolfgang von Hesse as the King of Finland. It requires Pehr Evind Svinhufvud to never leave office until the focus is completed. This also forms the ⟦2⟧ if it has already formed ⟦3⟧. This focus requires ⟦4⟧
The shared ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ sub-branch gives expansion opportunities in the Baltics, Penal divisions, and the creation of ⟦2⟧ or the ⟦3⟧ if Finland is a ⟦4⟧.

This branch allows Finland to possibly launch a civil war to become ⟦0⟧ and allows it to join the Axis, or create a Nordic faction. Finland can then demand the annexation of other Nordic countries in its faction. It also gives the national spirit ⟦1⟧ which increases military strength. This branch requires ⟦2⟧
This branch upgrades Finnish industry and resources. It also allows the use of Molotov Cocktails.
This branch upgrades the Finnish military and gives special national spirits for each branch.
This gives bonuses to the Finnish Army and gives an upgrades the national spirit ⟦0⟧
This hidden focus requires the player to complete the focuses ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ to become visible. It gives a super heavy tank variant in the designer. hidden focus requires ⟦2⟧
This gives bonuses to the Finnish Air Force and gives an upgrades the national spirit ⟦0⟧
This gives bonuses to the Finnish Navy and gives an upgrades the national spirit ⟦0⟧
This is the joint branch for the five Nordic nations. When a Nordic country creates a faction with another, this branch allows any Nordic faction member to complete any focus.
⟦0⟧ begins with 3 research slots available; 2 more can be unlocked through the national focus tree.
